newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Judge demands evidence from S.Africa's truth probe.
newsitem.headline: Judge demands evidence from S.Africa's truth probe.

text.p: A South African judge at the murder trial of an apartheid-era assassin on Monday ordered the country's truth commission to release testimony given to it in secret.

Lawyers for the former commander of the covert Vlakplaas police unit near Pretoria, Dirk Coetzee, had subpoenaed the Truth and Reconciliation Commission for the testimony by Joe Mamasela, who had worked as an informer at the unit.
The commission initially refused to hand over the information as it was given "in camera" or behind closed doors.
But Judge Piet Combrinck ordered the commission to release the testimony, saying Coetzee was entitled to the information under constitutional guarantees of the right to a free and fair trial.

"I find it astonishing that the very people who are charged to investigate the violation of human rights have shown such a callous indifference to the rights of others, and particularly the accused in this matter," Combrinck said in his ruling.
"I will certainly not make any order that will restrict this information," he added.
Lawyers for the truth body were expected to comply with the judge's order by handing over the evidence on Tuesday.
Mamasela is the state's key witness in the trial against Coetzee, a self-confessed assassin, for the 1981 murder of human rights lawyer Griffiths Mxenge.

The commission, which finishes its work at the end of this year, was set up to try to heal South Africa's divided past by investigating human rights abuses committed by all sides during 30 years of white minority rule.
It is able to grant amnesty to perpetrators who come forward and give full and honest accounts of their deeds.

Coetzee and two of his four co-accused, Almond Nofomela and David Tshikalanga, applied to the commission last year for amnesty for the brutal murder of Mxenge, whose family has waged a vociferous campaign against amnesty for his killers.
A decision on their amnesty request is expected in June.
